name: Umami Cloud
tagline: Open-source privacy analytics with a hosted cloud option

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-08-07; free Hobby tier, paid is Pro at $20/month for 1M events.
pricing.freeTier: The free Hobby plan covers 100k events a month on 3 sites with 6 months retention.

verdictSummary: The software is open source, so the cloud subscription is mostly paying for managed hosting, upgrades, and not touching a server.
coreLoopDIY: Self-host Umami, install the tracking script, create websites/events, and maintain database backups.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because analytics is not worth waking up to fix.

priorArt.name: Umami
priorArt.desc: The product's own open-source analytics platform.

alternatives.name: GoatCounter
alternatives.desc: The lighter self-hosted substitute when page traffic is the whole question.

facts.install: Create a hosted account or run the single static binary or Docker image
facts.dataFormat: A self-hosted instance uses SQLite by default or PostgreSQL; the hosted service stores analytics on GoatCounter's infrastructure and supports JSON and CSV exports
facts.gapVsPaid: It is lighter but much narrower in events, funnels, journeys and team analysis than Umami Cloud.
facts.setupBlocker: None for hosted use; self-hosting needs a reachable binary or container plus a public URL and TLS

alternatives.name: Plausible Community Edition
alternatives.desc: A similarly restrained privacy dashboard with a mature self-hosted edition.

facts.install: Deploy the Community Edition with the official Docker Compose installer
facts.dataFormat: Account and configuration records live in PostgreSQL and analytics events live in ClickHouse on the user's server
facts.gapVsPaid: It is similarly privacy-focused, but less flexible for journeys and product analytics and requires the user to operate the stack.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker Compose, roughly 2 GB of RAM, a domain with DNS and TLS, and backups for PostgreSQL and ClickHouse

alternatives.name: Rybbit
alternatives.desc: A broader self-hosted alternative with replay and funnels, at the cost of more moving parts.

facts.install: Use the hosted service or deploy the free self-hosted edition with Docker Compose
facts.dataFormat: The self-hosted stack uses PostgreSQL for application data, ClickHouse for analytics and Redis for queues and cache; hosted data lives in Rybbit's cloud
facts.gapVsPaid: It is newer and heavier, with less proven hosted reliability and more moving parts than Umami Cloud.
facts.setupBlocker: The indefinitely free path is self-hosting, which requires Docker Compose, a domain, secrets and enough resources for three data services

alternatives.name: Umami
alternatives.desc: Exactly Umami, except the cloud engineer is now you and Docker gets a vote.

facts.install: Create an Umami Cloud account or deploy the Node application with Docker Compose and PostgreSQL
facts.dataFormat: A self-hosted deployment stores analytics and account data in PostgreSQL; Umami Cloud stores it in Umami's managed service
facts.gapVsPaid: It is the same open-source core, but uptime, backups, upgrades and capacity planning move from Umami's team to the user.
facts.setupBlocker: None for hosted signup; self-hosting requires Docker or Node hosting and a PostgreSQL database

notes: Clean yes; good example of hosted open-source economics.
prompt:
Build me a self-hosted analytics stack to replace Umami Cloud. Requirements:

- Do not write analytics code. Umami is open source, deploy the real thing: a
  docker-compose.yml with the official umami image + postgres:15, data in a named
  volume. The subscription pays for hosting, so the build is a deployment.
- All secrets in .env: postgres password and Umami APP_SECRET. Umami binds to
  localhost; Caddy reverse-proxies stats.<mydomain> to it with automatic HTTPS.
- backup.sh on a nightly cron: pg_dump to ~/backups/umami-YYYY-MM-DD.sql.gz, keep
  14, with the restore command documented next to it.
- update.sh: pull the new image, restart, and print the release-notes URL so I can
  check for breaking changes before upgrading.
- Add the tracking script tag to my sites and verify pageviews arrive; create one
  custom event as proof the event pipeline works.
- No third-party telemetry; visitor data stays in my postgres.
- Out of scope: modifying Umami itself or building custom dashboards on top. And
  accept the honest cost: uptime, upgrades, and 2am breakage are mine now.
- README: DNS record for the stats subdomain, first-login default credentials, and
  change the admin password immediately.
